checks: Matched the frozen statement and proof to source 2a5bf571e6159901 §3 (3)–(8), §4, and §§5–6, including the facet variant. With unit mass, the midpoint cap leaves at least 1−3q among the vertices, and the three midpoints plus the first vertex leave at least 1−4q among the other two.

The determinant-one anchor is centered at a selected point. The affine interpolation of the three selected vertex points vanishes at that anchor and changes only fiber translations. Dividing the anchor's radius by two and its volume by 2^d in the cone estimate gives T. The other two vertex radii are at most 2T, and the half of the second positive vertex gives the last midpoint radius at most R_*/2.

Verified the six-site lattice census and width one under deletion of each of the three possible vertices. The three midpoints remain noncollinear, so width cannot be zero. Every midpoint gets positive volume by translating half of at least one of the two selected positive vertices.

Fixed-coefficient convex combinations pass to the exact integer sections. Fiber indicators converge in L1 on the bounded support, including null limit fibers. Closed pure-base caps are unchanged by mark motion, while all nonvertical caps have the same slab modulus at fixed base. Total variation then gives both depth limit inequalities at actual marks.

The centroid bound gives the same fixed q=1/4−ε/γ_d for every family in the sublevel, and if q<1/6 that sublevel is empty. A positive facet limit retains a fixed inner ball and is the intersection of the limiting rows by mixing toward the ball center. Null limits are explicitly admissible.

dependencies.mapping: Use the independent proof paragraphs on a single positive anchor and on B⊂L. The selected subsets at each midpoint have the required positive lower mass and known ball radius, and each target has upper mass q. No all-positive-fibers hypothesis of its main propagation statement is used.

Use the centroid halfspace inequality in proof (4) on each positive full d-fiber of the canonical ambient hull. A through-centroid ambient cap has either a containing ordinary fiber cap or the full own fiber, including pure-base normals.

Apply its null-fiber deletion statement to the exact convex-hull sections over the complete six-site P, with positive unit total measure. It preserves the measured trace and maximum depth, and the width calculation is separate.

overlap.comparison: The proof supplies the determinant-one anchor and cone radius formulas. Its propagation statement assumes a uniform positive volume floor for every fiber, whereas this theorem allows one null vertex and propagates through the six specified incidences.

The fixed-base total-variation and slab argument appears there with a fine-lattice limit, but it starts from bounded convergent fibers. It does not supply the six-fiber common affine normalization or the quarter-mass bound.

readability: The constant R_* includes a harmless factor of two. The fixed-sublevel assertion is vacuous if its q falls below 1/6.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the exact frozen candidate, original source comparison, accepted and same-batch dependency checks, and exact arithmetic where applicable.
summary: The explicit affine normalization bounds all six actual fibers. The Hausdorff limit is compatible, preserves mass and maximum depth, and has at most one null vertex. Both attainment conclusions follow.
